parole.significato: A level of administrative division used in Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia, and Singapore.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Malay mukim, from Arabic مُقِيم (muqīm, “resident”).

parole.significato: A crudely-built hut in parts of Asia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Malay pondok, borrowed from Arabic فُنْدُق (funduq), borrowed from Ancient Greek πανδοκεῖον (pandokeîon), from πᾰν- (păn-, “all, every”) + δοκ- (dok-, o-grade of the stem of δέχομαι (dékhomai, “to receive”)) + -εῖον (-eîon).

parole.significato: Malay poetry that is made up of four-line stanzas
parole.testo: From Malay syair, from Arabic شَاعِر (šāʕir, “poet”).
